Silence drawer never opens for prom-only rules

RuleActionsButtons now supports promRule-only usage for the ruler-less list view and AlertRuleMenu can show Silence via the Grafana prom ability, but the drawer is rendered only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. When rule (rulerRule) is undefined the condition is false, so clicking Silence sets showSilenceDrawer=true but renders nothing. The silence flow is broken for Grafana rules in the list view.

false_positives.candidate:
Cloud prom-only rules lose all actions

getEditableIdentifier only constructs an identifier from a ruler rule or a Grafana prom rule. For a datasource/cloud promRule without a rulerRule it logs a warning and returns undefined, and the component returns null early. That removes the entire More menu including non-edit actions like Copy link and Silence that should remain available for cloud rules. Previously rule was required so an identifier always existed.

Federated rule immutability check removed

useAllRulerRuleAbilities previously set isFederated via isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) and treated federated rules as immutable (no Update/Delete/Pause). The PR hardcodes isFederated=false with a TODO. Federated groups will now report Update/Delete/Pause as supported, allowing edit/delete UI on rules that cannot be edited.

Grafana prom abilities leak Duplicate permission to non-Grafana/undefined rules

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities with rule undefined (used when skipToken is passed for non-Grafana rules) still computes Duplicate as [MaybeSupported, grafana create permission]. If the user has Grafana create permission, AlertRuleMenu's OR logic (ruler OR grafana) makes canDuplicate true even for a Mimir/Loki cloud rule that should be gated only by its own ruler abilities. The hook should return NotSupported when rule is undefined/skipToken.

Pause/Delete actions gated on rulerRule, unreachable in prom-only list view

canPause/canDelete/canSilence/canDuplicate/canExport are now OR-ed between ruler abilities and Grafana prom abilities to support the ruler-less list view, but rendering still requires rulerRule: Pause item requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) and Delete block requires rulerRule &&. When the caller passes only promRule (rulerRule undefined, the new list-view case) the abilities can be true yet no Pause or Delete menu item is rendered. handleDelete also still takes (rule: RulerRuleDTO, groupIdentifier), so deletion cannot work without a ruler object.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

false_positives.candidate:
Early interpolation defeats $__range no-split guard

runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() before partitioning into splitting/non-splitting queries. querySupportsSplitting() explicitly excludes queries containing a range variable because interpolating $__range per split is wrong. If applyTemplateVariables replaces $__range/$__timeRange, the expr no longer contains the variable when querySupportsSplitting/isQueryWithRangeVariable runs, so range-variable queries will now be split and each split will get a baked-in full-range value instead of being left unsplit.

Range-dependent macros frozen to full range before time-splitting

Interpolating at the start uses request.range/intervalMs for the whole time range. Split sub-requests later get smaller ranges with the already-interpolated expr/step (e.g. $__auto, $__interval, $__rate_interval). Those macros should be evaluated per split partition, not once upfront, otherwise step/interval baked from the full range is reused for every 1-day chunk.

Template variables/filters applied twice in shard path

runShardSplitQuery interpolates with datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) and then delegates each shard group to runSplitQuery(), which now interpolates again with the same scopedVars/filters. A second applyTemplateVariables pass can double-apply ad-hoc filters from request.filters and re-replace already interpolated expr/step, corrupting the sharded selector produced by interpolateShardingSelector.

true_positives.golden_comment: The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
LoggerMiddleware loses traceID and depends on outer middleware

logRequest no longer adds pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName/dsUID and traceID explicitly and instead relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info. The contextual attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, etc.) are only added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware, and traceID is added nowhere: instrumentContext in contextual_logger_middleware.go does not add traceID, and the old tracing.TraceIDFromContext logic was deleted. If LoggerMiddleware is used standalone, in tests, or in a different order, logs lose those fields, and in the current stack trace correlation via traceID is regressed even when ordering is correct.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TestLogger.FromContext discards logs

TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand new NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver. LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so when the injected logger is a TestLogger the Info call is recorded on a throwaway instance that is immediately discarded. Any test asserting on InfoLogs/WarnLogs on the original fake will see zero calls and cannot verify logging behavior.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

false_positives.candidate:
Metrics middleware panics on nil request

QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics unconditionally dereference req (e.g. req.Queries, req.PluginContext, req.Body) without a nil guard. LoggerMiddleware in the same package explicitly short-circuits when req == nil. A nil request through MetricsMiddleware therefore panics with a nil-pointer dereference instead of delegating to the next client.

Shared MetricsMiddleware instance mutates next

NewMetricsMiddleware creates one imw via newMetricsMiddleware and the returned ClientMiddlewareFunc does imw.next = next; return imw on every application. The same *MetricsMiddleware value is therefore shared and mutated. If the middleware decorates more than one client or is constructed concurrently, the last next wins and concurrent QueryData/CallResource calls race on the next field. NewContextualLoggerMiddleware in the same PR correctly creates a fresh struct per application; MetricsMiddleware should do the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Check-then-act race allows device limit bypass

File pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go CreateOrUpdateDevice first does CountDevices and then either updateDevice or INSERT in separate transactions/sessions with no lock or unique constraint enforcement. Concurrent anonymous logins can both observe count < limit and both INSERT, exceeding the configured device_limit. The limit is therefore not reliably enforced under concurrency.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Expired devices can never re-register once limit reached

File pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go: CountDevices counts only devices updated within anonymousDeviceExpiration, but updateDevice also requires WHERE updated_at BETWEEN expiration and now. A returning device whose row expired and was not yet cleaned up will match zero rows and get ErrDeviceLimitReached instead of being re-inserted/updated, permanently locking out that device ID even though it should be treated as a new slot after expiration.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

false_positives.candidate:
Shared mutable cached pointer returned without copy

In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets caches a *dtos.EntryPointAssets in a global and returns the same pointer to all callers on the fast path. The mutex only protects the global pointer itself, not the pointed-to struct/slices. Anyone reading only this finding should understand: if any caller mutates the returned object (for example calling SetContentDeliveryURL or appending to JSFiles), those writes race with concurrent readers of the same shared object and the race detector will still fire despite the new mutex. The consequence is a remaining data race / cross-request corruption. Fix by treating the cached value as immutable, returning a deep copy, or documenting and enforcing no mutation by callers.

Write lock held across file and network I/O

In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() and then does readWebAssetsFromFile and readWebAssetsFromCDN while still holding it (defer Unlock). A write lock on a sync.RWMutex blocks all RLock readers, so every concurrent cache hit that should take the fast RLock path at the top of the function will block for the duration of the file read or HTTP fetch. The consequence is unnecessary serialization, latency spikes and thread pile-up under load. Load outside the lock (with double-check/singleflight) and only hold the lock to publish the result.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The enableSqlExpressions function has flawed logic that always returns false, effectively disabling SQL expressions unconditionally:
The DB methods NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/db.go return hardcoded 'not implemented' errors after removing the go-duck dependency.

false_positives.candidate:
Index out of range panic on empty AST

In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go function tablesFromAST does flatten.Flatten(ast[0], ...) without checking len(ast). If TablesList ever returns an empty JSON array (e.g. valid SQL with no statement, serialization returning []) the code panics with index out of range, crashing the handler/goroutine and causing denial of service. The caller TablesList never validates that the unmarshalled slice is non-empty before calling it.

Vulnerable SQL string interpolation left in disabled code

In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go TablesList builds a SQL command with fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL) after only doubling single quotes. The PR stubs the DB so it is not currently reachable, but the vulnerable construction is left in place. If the stub is ever replaced with a real implementation the injection returns. Disabled security-sensitive code should be removed, not left dormant.

true_positives.golden_comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
No per-key guard allows duplicate concurrent BuildIndex for same key

The change removed the global cacheMu lock around the whole BuildIndex and now only locks around the final b.cache[key] = idx assignment. Two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource (e.g. from init workers plus getOrCreateIndex on a concurrent Search) will both create a bleve index, run the builder, and overwrite each other. For file-backed indexes bleve.New on the same directory will fail or lock, turning a duplicate-build inefficiency into user-visible Search errors. Fix with per-key singleflight/mutex so only one build per key runs at a time.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TotalDocs reads cache map without lock causing data race

bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates b.cache directly with no b.cacheMu.RLock, while BuildIndex now inserts into b.cache under b.cacheMu.Lock concurrently and GetIndex reads under RLock. Concurrent map read+write is a fatal data race/panic in Go. The finer-grain locking in BuildIndex made this reachable during parallel startup builds. Fix by holding RLock around the iteration and DocCount collection.

false_positives.candidate:
Data race on counter and loop variable in concurrent index init

In searchSupport.init the for _, info := range stats loop launches group.Go(func() error { ... info ...; totalBatchesIndexed++ ... }) with concurrency up to initWorkers. totalBatchesIndexed is a plain int incremented from multiple goroutines with no atomic/mutex, which is a data race and corrupts the indexed count reported in the span event. The closure also captures the loop variable info; on Go versions before per-iteration scoping this builds the wrong namespace/group/resource concurrently. Fix by copying info into a loop-local variable and using an atomic counter.

History/Origin panic when search is not configured

Server.History calls s.search.History and Server.Origin calls s.search.Origin with no nil check, while Server.Search does check s.search == nil. When the server is constructed without Search.Resources, s.search is nil, so any History or Origin RPC dereferences a nil pointer and panics the gRPC server instead of returning an error. Add the same not-configured guard as Search.

Search watch goroutine leaks and busy-loops on closed channel

searchSupport.init creates watchctx := context.Background() with no cancel and loops with v := <-events calling s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) without checking ok. The channel returned by WatchWriteEvents is closed on backend shutdown, at which point the receive returns the zero value immediately forever, causing a hot infinite loop indexing nil events, and the poller tied to the discarded context can never be stopped. Fix by deriving watchctx from the server lifecycle context with cancel and breaking on !ok.

false_negatives.golden_comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.
Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

false_positives.candidate:
Login cache not invalidated by organization-side changes

In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java getForLogin() caches IDP id sets per realm+FetchMode+organizationId, but invalidation is only registered from IdentityProviderStorageProvider.create/update/remove. Organization-side mutations that change the same result set - linking/unlinking an IDP to an org, removing an org, disabling/enabling an org, toggling org membership visibility - go through OrganizationProvider and never invalidate cacheKeyForLogin. The cached id list is then resolved via getById and returned, showing IDPs from the wrong org or showing IDPs whose org was removed/disabled as still available for login.

Login predicate NPEs when IDP config is null

In IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java line 254 getLoginPredicate() does idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(...)). If an IdentityProviderModel has a null config map and a non-null organizationId, idp.getConfig().get() throws NullPointerException. The predicate is now called on create/remove/update paths in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider to decide login-cache invalidation, so a null-config org-linked IDP breaks those writes instead of just skipping invalidation. Use a null-safe access such as getConfig() == null check or getOrDefault.

remove() NPEs when alias does not exist

In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java remove() unconditionally does storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) then registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) when the alias key is invalidated. registerIDPInvalidation dereferences idp.getInternalId() and idp.getAlias(). If no IDP exists for the alias, storedIdp is null and the remove of a non-existent alias throws NullPointerException instead of returning false. The old code had the same pattern but the new code also passes storedIdp to registerIDPLoginInvalidation, widening the path. Guard for null before invalidating.

removeAll() does not invalidate login caches

In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java removeAll() only calls registerCountInvalidation() and explicitly skips per-entry invalidation. The new getForLogin() cache keyed by cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode) is therefore left populated after all IDPs are deleted, so subsequent getForLogin() calls can return stale IDs until natural eviction or until the fallback getById miss path fires. The method must also register invalidation for each FetchMode login key.

update() NPEs when IDP id is unknown

In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java update() does IdentityProviderModel idpById = getById(model.getInternalId()) then registerIDPInvalidation(idpById) and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model) without a null check. getById returns null when the internalId does not exist. registerIDPInvalidation immediately calls idp.getInternalId(), so updating a non-existent or already-removed IDP throws NullPointerException instead of delegating to storage. Add a null guard.

true_positives.golden_comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getBouncyCastleProvider returns unrelated KeyStore provider

AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is typically SUN/JKS, not BouncyCastle. Callers expect a BouncyCastle (or BCFIPS) provider and use it for BC-specific algorithms and BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER logic. Returning an arbitrary JCA provider is misleading and will cause NoSuchAlgorithm/NoSuchProvider failures or wrong algorithm behavior when the authz provider is selected.

true_positives.golden_comment: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dead discarded ASN1Encoder writes

concatenatedRSToASN1DER() contains two lines ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger) and ...write(sBigInteger) whose results are discarded immediately before building the real sequence. They are dead code left over from development and should be removed to avoid confusion about encoding.

true_positives.golden_comment: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations
true_positives.matched_candidate:
New abstract order() breaks all existing CryptoProvider implementations

CryptoProvider.order() is added as an abstract method with no default. Any third-party or downstream implementation of CryptoProvider that compiled against the old interface will fail with AbstractMethodError / NoSuchMethodError at runtime and fail to compile. For backward compatibility this should be a default method (e.g. default int order() { return 0; }).

false_negatives.golden_comment: When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.

false_positives.candidate:
Crypto init uses class loader instead of context class loader

AuthzClient.create() calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()). ServiceLoader detection in modular, OSGi, shaded-client, or app-server environments typically needs the thread context class loader. Using the defining loader can fail to discover the Default/Elytron/FIPS provider or discover a different set than the rest of Keycloak, making provider selection environment-dependent.

ECDSA conversion silently truncates/pads negative or oversized integers

integerToBytes() converts BigInteger r/s to fixed length by truncating leading bytes or zero-padding with no range check. A negative BigInteger (from new BigInteger(bytes) interpreting high-bit as sign) or a value >= 2^(8*qLength) is silently wrapped instead of rejected. DER signatures must have 0 < r,s < n; accepting/rewriting out-of-range values breaks verification semantics and can hide malformed/forged signatures.

First-init-wins + ordering can lock server to weak authz provider

CryptoIntegration.init() is a no-op once cryptoProvider is set. AuthzClient.create() calls init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()). If an authz-client operation runs first in a VM that later hosts the server, the low-priority AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100, most methods throw UnsupportedOperationException) becomes the global provider and full providers (order 200) are never adopted. Conversely standalone authz-client use gets a provider where signature/keyfactory/cert operations all throw. Initialization order therefore silently determines correctness.

Signed BigInteger parsing of DER INTEGER

ASN1Decoder.readInteger() uses new BigInteger(bytes), which interprets bytes as two's-complement signed. DER INTEGERs for ECDSA r/s are unsigned and use a leading zero for the high-bit case. A malicious encoding without the leading zero becomes negative instead of being rejected, and flows into integerToBytes() above. It should use new BigInteger(1, bytes) plus explicit range validation.

Test uses P-256 key for ES384/ES512 so curve coverage is fake

The test fixture generates one KeyPair with KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair(), which defaults to secp256r1/P-256. testES384 and testES512 then sign with that P-256 key but convert with algorithm.getSignatureLength() of 96/132. The conversion round-trip rsConcat->DER->rsConcat holds for any length due to pad/truncate logic, so the tests pass without ever exercising real P-384/P-521 keys, DER sizes, or JCA verification.

true_positives.golden_comment: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing null-check and missing all-clients fallback causes NPE / deny

Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

Removal listener can throw UnsupportedOperationException under V2

false_positives.candidate:
Feature flag only enabled for explicit strategy, default case left disabled

In createInitialDeployment() the method returns early when updateStrategy == null before enabling the rolling-updates feature. Consequence is lost mutual exclusion for a partition, corrupting all_offsets/outstanding sets and causing wrong committable offsets, stalls, or duplicate/lost commits.

Offsets committed from background thread

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy spawns a commit_thread that calls the Arroyo Commit object every second via commit_function, outside poll/submit/join. Arroyo Commit/StreamProcessor commit paths are not designed for concurrent calls from user threads and interact with rebalance/close lifecycle. Consequence is races with partition revocation, commits after revoke, duplicate commits, or crashes, plus leaked commit threads when strategies are recreated.

Single shared queue pool reused across rebalances

ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and every create_with_partitions returns a new SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy sharing that pool and its OffsetTracker, each with its own commit thread. On rebalance Arroyo closes the old strategy, whose close() shuts down the shared pool out from under the new strategy, and old commit threads are never stopped. Consequence is workers killed after rebalance, stuck processing, double commits, and assert failures once shutdown() sets queue_pool to None.

Consequence is premature test assertions and, if reused for shutdown/commit gating, committing or shutting down too early.

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit decodes then asserts isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue), while decoder decode_payload asserts payload is not FilteredPayload. A FilteredPayload therefore triggers an AssertionError caught by the generic except that logs Error submitting message to queue and then marks the offset complete. Consequence is noisy exception logs for normal filtered messages and, for any non-BrokerValue message, the offset is never tracked at all, permanently blocking contiguous commit for that partition.

In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() and then does readWebAssetsFromFile and readWebAssetsFromCDN while still holding it (defer Unlock). false_positives.candidate:
Unsanitized raw_html rendered with raw

In app/views/embed/best.html.erb the template outputs <%= raw post.cooked %>. Combined with the new Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] path, cooked is arbitrary remote HTML from RSS/Readability stored verbatim without cooking or sanitization. Any compromised feed or fetched page yields persistent JavaScript execution in the embed iframe and in any other place the post is displayed.

Wrong default for cook_method makes all posts raw_html

In db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb the column is added with default: 1, null: false. Post.cook_methods is Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html), so regular is 0 and raw_html is 1. Every existing and future post without an explicit value becomes raw_html, so Post#cook returns raw uncooked HTML instead of cooked output, breaking rendering and bypassing sanitization site-wide. Default should be the regular value.

Unvalidated open(url) allows SSRF/LFI and DoS

In app/models/topic_embed.rb import_remote does open(url).read with no scheme validation, timeout, size limit, or rescue. It is reachable from TopicRetriever with user-supplied embed_url, from PollFeed with feed item links, and from the disqus importer. open-uri follows redirects, so internal hosts/metadata endpoints can be fetched, local file wrappers or pipe metacharacters may be abused depending on Ruby version, large bodies exhaust memory, and network errors raise unhandled exceptions that fail jobs.

raw_html cook path skips sanitization pipeline

In app/models/post.rb Post#cook returns raw verbatim when cook_method is raw_html, skipping PrettyText cooking and sanitization. Since TopicEmbed creates/updates posts with skip_validations and this cook method from remote content, malicious HTML/JS is preserved and later served as cooked, enabling stored XSS wherever the post excerpt or body is shown outside the embed iframe.

Invalid X-Frame-Options value

In app/controllers/embed_controller.rb ensure_embeddable sets response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL". ALLOWALL is not a valid X-Frame-Options directive; browsers treat unknown values as DENY or ignore framing inconsistently, which can break legitimate embeds. To allow framing, the header should be removed or ALLOW-FROM with the specific origin should be used where supported.

Non-atomic throttle key and unbounded URL key

In lib/topic_retriever.rb retrieved_recently? uses $redis.setnx followed by separate expire, which is not atomic. If the process crashes between calls the key never expires and that URL is throttled forever. The key is "retrieved:#{@embed_url}" with raw user input, so an attacker varying query strings creates unlimited keys and unlimited RetrieveTopic jobs, bypassing the per-URL 60s throttle and enabling Sidekiq/network flooding.

If `convert`/`gifsicle` fails or is killed mid-write, the original upload is corrupted/truncated, and the loop will pointlessly retry the same failing conversion up to 5 times. false_positives.candidate:
Wrong dayjs.tz overload for UTC offset

Line 107 computes `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()`. That overload parses `date.start` as wall-time in `organizerTimeZone` instead of converting the instant to that zone. The correct form is `dayjs(date.start).tz(organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()`. The current code yields a bogus offset (dependent on system TZ and double-interpretation), so date-override day matching and in/out checks are shifted by hours.

Near midnight or with non-UTC organizers the UTC weekday/hour maps to the wrong working-hours entry, accepting slots outside hours and rejecting valid ones.

Line 207 selects `activeOverrides` by `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, ...)` without converting the override instant to invitee wall-time. Because the name does not match, the hook is never called and `website_name` is always serialized, even when `website` is blank (as nil), adding noise to the payload and defeating the intended `website.present?` guard.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the main issue in the golden comment: include_website_name is missing the '?' suffix, so ActiveModel::Serializer never calls the conditional hook. It does not mention the string mutation concern, but the core issue matches.

false_positives.candidate:
`website_name` leaks for TL0 users seen as anonymous

File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb adds `:website_name` to the serialized `attributes` list but does not add it to the `untrusted_attributes` list (`bio_raw`, `website`, `location`, etc.). The custom `include_website_name` guard only checks `website.present?` and does not check `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. Therefore an anonymous viewer of a TL0 user will have `website` suppressed but will still receive `website_name` (derived directly from the hidden website), leaking the private host/path the restriction was meant to hide. The spec's `untrusted_attributes` array has the same omission.

Repeated unrescued URI parsing can raise and drops port/query

File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb in `website_name` rescues `URI(website.to_s).host` with `rescue nil` but then calls `URI(website.to_s).path` two more times without rescue. A malformed `website` value that returns nil host on the first parse will raise `URI::InvalidURIError` on the later parses, turning a profile render into a 500. Even for valid URLs the display is lossy: only `host + path` is kept, so port (`example.com:8080`), query string, and fragment are silently dropped, and a site-relative or scheme-less value yields nil host so the link disappears in the template even though `model.website` exists.

Additionally the full referer URL including path is used as targetOrigin instead of scheme://host:port, so legitimate messages fail origin checks.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate leads with an XSS concern, but it also states that the full referer URL is used as targetOrigin instead of scheme://host:port, which makes legitimate messages fail. That is the golden issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Unsanitized raw_html rendered with raw

In app/views/embed/best.html.erb the template outputs <%= raw post.cooked %>. Combined with the new Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] path, cooked is arbitrary remote HTML from RSS/Readability stored verbatim without cooking or sanitization. Any compromised feed or fetched page yields persistent JavaScript execution in the embed iframe and in any other place the post is displayed.

Wrong default for cook_method makes all posts raw_html

In db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb the column is added with default: 1, null: false. Post.cook_methods is Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html), so regular is 0 and raw_html is 1. Every existing and future post without an explicit value becomes raw_html, so Post#cook returns raw uncooked HTML instead of cooked output, breaking rendering and bypassing sanitization site-wide. Default should be the regular value.

Unvalidated open(url) allows SSRF/LFI and DoS

In app/models/topic_embed.rb import_remote does open(url).read with no scheme validation, timeout, size limit, or rescue. It is reachable from TopicRetriever with user-supplied embed_url, from PollFeed with feed item links, and from the disqus importer. open-uri follows redirects, so internal hosts/metadata endpoints can be fetched, local file wrappers or pipe metacharacters may be abused depending on Ruby version, large bodies exhaust memory, and network errors raise unhandled exceptions that fail jobs.

raw_html cook path skips sanitization pipeline

In app/models/post.rb Post#cook returns raw verbatim when cook_method is raw_html, skipping PrettyText cooking and sanitization. Since TopicEmbed creates/updates posts with skip_validations and this cook method from remote content, malicious HTML/JS is preserved and later served as cooked, enabling stored XSS wherever the post excerpt or body is shown outside the embed iframe.

Invalid X-Frame-Options value

In app/controllers/embed_controller.rb ensure_embeddable sets response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL". ALLOWALL is not a valid X-Frame-Options directive; browsers treat unknown values as DENY or ignore framing inconsistently, which can break legitimate embeds. To allow framing, the header should be removed or ALLOW-FROM with the specific origin should be used where supported.

Non-atomic throttle key and unbounded URL key

In lib/topic_retriever.rb retrieved_recently? uses $redis.setnx followed by separate expire, which is not atomic. If the process crashes between calls the key never expires and that URL is throttled forever. The key is "retrieved:#{@embed_url}" with raw user input, so an attacker varying query strings creates unlimited keys and unlimited RetrieveTopic jobs, bypassing the per-URL 60s throttle and enabling Sidekiq/network flooding.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The retry loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` using the same path for source and destination and discards the boolean return value. true_positives.reasoning: Both point out that dayjs objects are compared with ===, which checks object identity rather than value, so the comparison is always false. They describe the same bug.

false_positives.candidate:
Wrong dayjs.tz overload for UTC offset

Line 107 computes `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()`. That overload parses `date.start` as wall-time in `organizerTimeZone` instead of converting the instant to that zone. The correct form is `dayjs(date.start).tz(organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()`. The current code yields a bogus offset (dependent on system TZ and double-interpretation), so date-override day matching and in/out checks are shifted by hours.

Line 207 selects `activeOverrides` by `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, ...)` without converting the override instant to invitee wall-time. The outer forEach is not awaited, so the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) at line 652 can run before pushes happen. Recurring-booking cancellations can therefore skip deleting external calendar events entirely and never surface errors.

Dynamic imports are eager, defeating lazy-loading intent

In packages/app-store/index.ts the object literal applecalendar: import("./applecalendar"), etc. executes every import() as soon as the module is evaluated, starting ~30 parallel chunk loads on every server boot/request path that imports appStore. Callers still await appStore[key], so correctness is preserved, but there is no on-demand loading. Use getters or functions returning import() to make loading truly lazy.
